Game mechanics, game play, perks, weapons, maps are decent +
Frankly no complaints, as the game delivers everything expected, not much more.

Where the game fails is that there is only 15 Missions, when you include the DLC.
If this game delivered 30 maps total (including DLCs) I would be able to reccomend this as a top Tier game!
Alien Fireteam Elite is indeed a really good game, just needs more content.
Problem being that while configuring your weapons and your builds are great fun, you have to play them on maps that are too repetitive. I have maxed out half of the classes and I am already bored of all the maps. We need DLCs containing lots more maps and or even more perks, fund it with some class DLCs or something, get to work!

And as a last note, imagine procedural generated maps, it would put this game up  with or above Vermintide and Dead By Daylight.

How can I say this... The game is worth your money, but its currently not worth your time?
I am sad to not be able to recommend it currently and I really hope this change in the future.. :-)
Fun game if just want to sit back and destroy hundreds of aliens.This game is for you. Especially if you're a fan of the alien franchise.

[h1][i]“A day in the Marine Corps is like a day on the farm.
Every meal's a banquet!”[/i]
~Sergeant Apone[/h1]

[b]Alien[/b] franchise is old. Can you even believe that the bloody thing was around since 70s? Yet it's one of those things that never die. Those that are always around. There's always something. Movies (just recently, we've got ourselves [b]Alien: Romulus[/b], which, despite all of its obvious problems, was quite good), comics, and, of course, video games. Shocking, I know. I mean, it's not unusual (shut up, [b]Carlton[/b]) for big franchises to have video game adaptations. Especially the old ones, since movie-based games were way more common in times when production was cheaper. But the thing is – it's a bit more interesting than usual with the [b]Alien[/b]. Think about it. Usually, the source defines adaptation. Right? I mean, it's hard to imagine [b]The Terminator[/b] to solve puzzles on [b]MYST[/b] island. But with [b]Alien[/b]? It's like we have not one but two radically different sources at this point.

The first one is, obviously, the original. 1979 [b]Ridley Scott[/b]'s philosophical horror. Say whatever you want, it was more about hidden meaning than scary creature killing [b]Nostromo[/b] crew. Which led us to [b]Prometheus[/b]. A movie that lots of people disliked because, well, it wasn't about killing. It was all [b]Graham Hancock[/b]. If you know what I mean. [b]Annunaki[/b] and sh*t. And... Let's just say at that point of time, it was not what audience wanted. Why? Well, because of our second source – 1986 movie [b]Aliens[/b]. Directed by the master of mainstream entertainment,[b]James Cameron[/b], it was exactly that – [i]entertainment[/i]. That's just what [b]Cameron[/b] does. He takes promising ideas and he makes them entertaining. He's kind of a genius in that field. An old [b]Harlan Ellison[/b]'s short story, for example, gave us [b]The Terminator[/b]. One of the most recognizable things in popular media.

And [b]Aliens[/b]? It was the same kind of stuff. What was it about? Well, it had space marines. Those were shooting aliens. That's it. That's the entire thing. There was nothing else. Sounds dumb and yes, it was dumb. Yet it was great. Why? Because [b]Cameron[/b], that's why. Think about second [b]Terminator[/b] movie. What was the meaning of it? Who cares! Screw the meaning, it had [b]Arnie[/b] on bike, helicopter chase and that CGI dude! Same thing with the [b]Aliens[/b]. It had [b]Sigourney Weaver[/b] fighting a huge [b]Xenomorph[/b] in that power loader, it had lots of monsters, and, of course, there were those memorable lines. Admit it, we all had one of those friends who kept screaming “[i]Game over, man! Game over![/i]” back then for every bloody occasion.

Why is all that important for us to understand? Because naturally, such a duality affects games. Look at that old [b]Alien[/b] game. No, not the first one, which was just a [b]Pac-Man[/b] clone for [b]Atari 2600[/b], the one that came out in 1984. It was a pretty complicated experience. We took control of [b]Nostromo[/b] and our goal was, naturally, to get rid of alien. Or escape on [b]Narcissus[/b] shuttlecraft, since game was non-linear and gave us lots of freedom. While going through more than 30 rooms, we were supposed to track [b]Xenomorph[/b] by using special tools, but guess what? [b]Xenomorph[/b] wasn't the only creature on board. [b]Jonesy[/b], the cat, was there too and our trackers? Those didn't know the difference. Therefore it was hard to tell what's moving – our furry friend or that living murder machine from space (where no one can hear you scream). It was a fun game that captured movie's atmosphere pretty well. Now, [b]Aliens[/b] movie comes and... Yeah. [b]KONAMI[/b]'s arcade. Quite awesome. Yet nothing but juicy shooting.

So, history aside. What kind of game is [b]Fireteam Elite[/b]? Well, obviously, it's [b]Cameron[/b], not [b]Scott[/b]. At least, that's what it tries to be. Don't expect it to be anything like [b]Alien: Isolation[/b]. Which was all [b]Scott[/b]. The idea here was to make one of those co-op shooters that are popular nowadays. People love such games, market is not overcrowded, while before [b]HELLDIVERS II[/b] dropped, there was a big chance for a solid new AAA project to take the lead. All we needed is a name to make people bother. [b]Alien[/b]? Was one of such names. So, here we are. Having one of them always-online shooters with [b]Xenomorphs[/b]. Yet nobody plays it. Why? Well, because it sucks. That's why.

See, the problem with this game is not the idea. The idea was fine, there's nothing wrong with it. If something, it made perfect sense for [b]Alien[/b] franchise to have something like that. The problem is – this here isn't a AAA game. That certain something that makes difference between one of them [b]Cameron[/b]'s hits and cheesy B-movies just isn't there. If something, this game feels indie. As far as I know, it's the very first game for its makers – [b]Cold Iron Studios[/b]. Most likely, you didn't even hear of 'em. So... Who are they? Well, the thing is – [b]Cold Iron[/b] is pretty much our ol' pals [b]Cryptic[/b]. [b]City of Heroes[/b], [b]Champions Online[/b], [b]Star Trek Online[/b], [b]Neverwinter[/b]... Those guys. An MMO crowd. [b]Cryptic[/b] is owned by the [b]Embracer Group[/b] now and at this point f*ckers fired pretty much everybody (games like [b]STO[/b] are moved to other teams who make living by keeping the old MMOs alive), so... Yeah. [b]Cold Iron Studios[/b]. And it's not a bad thing. At least our guys had experience, right? Unfortunately, that didn't help 'em. They didn't need the experience here. They needed [i]budget[/i]. Think about it. There are two approaches on such games. You can go cheap and make [b]Deep Rock Galactic[/b], or you can go expensive and make [b]HELLDIVERS II[/b]. Both games knew their nature, both ended up being cool for what they are. [b]Fireteam Elite[/b]? It has budget of [b]Deep Rock[/b], yet it tries to be [b]HELLDIVERS[/b]. Should I say that things just don't work that way?

The good thing about this game is that it'll run on a toaster. Pretty old one too. Which is always a good thing for an online-only game (no idea what [b]BLIZZARD[/b] were thinking while making their [b]Diablo IV[/b] so demanding). Doesn't look too bad either. I mean, it's far from looking [i]good[/i], but you know. It's tolerable. The real problem is – there's close to no content here. Single player campaign and multiplayer are merged into the same exact thing and that thing has only four episodes, three short missions each. You know the drill. Clear the room, assemble, repeat. For 12 times. Because after that? There's nothing. Well, aside from DLC, but even if you'll pay for all bells and whistles, you'll only get some ugly skins and one extra episode. Yes, only one episode. That's it.

And yes, after such a long introduction, that's pretty much everything I have to say about this game. That it's cheap and somewhat playable game with close to no content or variety in it. Even [b]Predator[/b] franchise did better in its [b]Hunting Grounds[/b]. I mean, running through the same dull maps again and again with no end? There's no way in Hell... I mean, [i]space[/i] you'll do that. Most likely, you'll just finish the story with bots (spoiler alert – even that doesn't worth it, since story is barely there) and that'll be the end of it for you. And it's both sad and weird. I mean, what went wrong? Why was it so hard to produce more maps? Even with quantity over quality approach, I can see myself staying longer if there were lots and lots of maps to choose from. I like the franchise, skill system (yes, it's the only interesting thing here to mention) is rather cute and, let's just admit it, it's nice to have an online game that'll run on your old laptop. But no. Not only they failed to make proper AAA impact, they didn't provide us with enough content. Which ultimately kills all the purpose. Dixi.

Fun with a group of friends, not so much solo. The last few updates have pretty much made this game less of a grind fest, easier to obtain challenge cards so you quickly power through the loot system. While it won't inspire any kind of horror, it does at least offer manic intense action moments that will remind you of those scenes from Aliens. Again, highly recommend playing this with friends, especially at later levels, as the AI is pretty brain dead. You'll pretty much find one weapon you really like and use that throughout the game, so don't go into this hoping there's some kind of deep gear system. But of all the Aliens games out there, this one is at least playable with short bursts of enjoyment. And if you can get it for the sale price, even better.
